title: Diarrhea
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea, bloating, abdominal pain, weight loss, fatigue, and iron deficiency anemia. Celiac disease is an autoimmune enteropathy triggered by gluten in genetically susceptible individuals (HLA-DQ2/DQ8). Gliadin peptides are deamidated by tissue transglutaminase (tTG) → immune response → small intestinal villous atrophy. Classic extra-intestinal manifestations: dermatitis herpetiformis (pruritic vesicles on extensor surfaces), iron deficiency anemia, osteoporosis, peripheral neuropathy. Diagnosis: IgA anti-tTG antibody (first-line serology) + total IgA level (rule out IgA deficiency, which causes false-negative tTG). If IgA deficient, use IgG anti-tTG or anti-DGP. Confirm with duodenal biopsy showing villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, intraepithelial lymphocytosis (gold standard). DO NOT start gluten-free diet before biopsy. Treatment: lifelong strict gluten-free diet. Monitor nutritional deficiencies (iron, B12, folate, vitamin D, calcium).
